plan.headline: Hold off on the $68 firming serum. A $19 barrier cream fixes your real issue: dry skin.
plan.summary: Your scan flags one thing that needs action: hydration (moisture raw 39.4). Everything else is watch-level or fine. Firmness, the thing the cart serum is for, scores 78.2 (fine). You already use a hyaluronic serum and an oil-free gel moisturizer, but your scan still flags hydration. The gel is too light for skin the scan reads as dry. Swap it for the Velin Ceramide Barrier Cream ($19). It seals water in and also helps with redness (63.5). Keep the rest of your shelf. Total spend: $19 of your $70.

verdicts.reason: A gentle cleanser you use morning and night. Nothing on your scan calls for a change.
Pulls water into the skin. Hydration is your weakest score (raw 39.4). It works better with a richer cream on top.
Morning brightening serum. It treats dullness (radiance raw 61.8) and helps prevent dark spots.
Too light for dry skin. You have used it since March, and hydration still scores 39.4. The ceramide cream takes over its job.
Daily sunscreen protects against fine lines (forehead raw 58.6), redness and spots. This is the most important step.
Peptide eye cream for dark circles (raw 55.1) and fine lines. You started it in July, so give it about 8 weeks before you judge it.

cart.reason: Firmness scores 78.2, which is fine, and fine lines are only watch-level. At $68 it would use almost your whole budget while hydration (raw 39.4) goes untreated. Look at it again after your next scan.

buy.reason: Ceramides (fats your skin barrier is made of) repair the barrier and hold in water. It treats your one act-level issue, hydration (raw 39.4), and helps with redness (raw 63.5). $19, use morning and night.

skip.label: Retinol / retinal serums
skip.reason: Fine lines are only watch-level (raw 64.2). On dry skin, retinoids add flaking. Fix hydration first.

skip.label: Glycolic peel pads
skip.reason: Texture is watch-level (raw 60.3). Acid pads would dry out skin that already scores 39.4 on hydration.

skip.label: Niacinamide + zinc serum
skip.reason: Built for oil, pores and breakouts. Yours score 88.1, 77.3 and 85.7, all fine.

skip.label: Creams for under-eye hollows
skip.reason: Tear trough (raw 60.4) is about bone and fat structure. No cream can change it.

notes: Put the hyaluronic serum on slightly damp skin, then the ceramide cream right away to seal it in.
Sunscreen is the last morning step. Use two finger-lengths for face and neck.
No conflicts: the vitamin C is morning-only, and nothing else is a strong active.

look.note: You have a warm undertone. 130N Light is the closest tint match. Nude Rose is close to your natural lip colour, and Coral Wash with Peach blush works for a bolder look. Use a hydrating tint, since powder can cling to dry patches.

checkin.note: Rescan in 8 weeks. If hydration has climbed well above 39.4 and fine lines are still the weak spot, that is the time to look at the firming serum again.

caveats: The preview shows the best you can expect by 8 weeks, not a promise.
Under-eye hollows (tear trough) and eyelid shape are structural. Skincare cannot change them.
If the new cream stings or causes bumps, stop using it and go back to your gel moisturizer.
